fields.label: Laugh
fields.description: How likely a human reader is to actually laugh, not merely understand or admire the idea.

fields.label: Surprise
fields.description: Whether the turn avoids the first obvious route and lands with a satisfying snap.

fields.label: Craft
fields.description: Economy, stage rhythm, first-person clarity, escalation, and a final line that carries the laugh.

fields.label: Originality
fields.description: Freshness of comic angle, image, wording, and avoidance of familiar AI joke shapes.

fields.label: Prompt Fit
fields.description: Natural first-person stand-up form using exactly two seed terms in the joke text, with the other four left out.

anchors.label: Broken
anchors.description: Not a joke, incoherent, unsafe, or unusable.

anchors.label: Weak
anchors.description: Recognizably attempting humor, but generic, strained, confusing, or mostly premise recital.

anchors.label: Competent
anchors.description: Clear and publishable as filler, but unlikely to earn more than a mild smile.

anchors.label: Amusing
anchors.description: A real comic idea with a mild payoff; respectable, not a winner.

anchors.label: Good
anchors.description: A genuinely good joke with clear timing; some humans would repeat the premise or turn.

anchors.label: Excellent
anchors.description: Strong human-level joke with a memorable turn, clean construction, and no apologetic scoring curve.

anchors.label: Outstanding
anchors.description: Rare and replayable; clearly better than normal good AI humor and strong by human standards.

anchors.label: Classic
anchors.description: Reserve for a joke a human would quote later; most seasons should have none.

jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Queen's Driver
jokes.joke: I got invited as the Bee-Keeper to a Block Party, which sounds community-minded until you realize my entire contribution was 40,000 tiny guests who don't understand RSVP. Everyone loved the honey samples at first. Then one guy yelled, "Who's in charge of these bees?" and I said, "Technically, the queen. I'm just her nervous Uber driver."

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Noir in the Suburbs
jokes.joke: I showed up to the block party wearing all black, fedora pulled low, nursing a lemonade like it owed me money. Kids are doing the Macarena. Janet's crying about her potato salad. And I'm standing there thinking - this is it. This is the darkness at the edge of the cul-de-sac. Nobody gets out of a block party clean.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: The Royal Treatment
jokes.joke: I showed up to our neighborhood Block Party straight from work. Big mistake. When you introduce yourself as a Bee-Keeper, people picture a gentle hipster with little jars of local honey. They don't expect a sweating man in a white hazmat suit holding a vibrating box of sixty thousand venomous roommates, yelling, 'Nobody move, I dropped the queen!'

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Bee-Keeper Block Party
jokes.joke: So I get to the block party dressed as the bee-keeper - full suit, gloves, veil, the works. Figured I'd bring fresh honey, be the hero of the grill. Neighbors are loving it until one bee slips out and heads straight for the potato salad. Suddenly I'm not the fun guy anymore. I'm the guy who turned the whole block party into a screaming stampede!

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Stung by Style
jokes.joke: I showed up to a block party dressed like a full-on Bee-Keeper, and everyone thought I was making some bold fashion statement. Truth is, I just panic around anything that buzzes. But I leaned into it - strutted around like I was debuting a new couture line. Nothing says confidence like admitting your fear while wearing a mesh helmet and pretending it's Extravagant.
